name: keening

attributes.attribute: invented keening after her son died
son of Brigit, killed in battle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Keening is an Irish ritual of mourning for the dead. It looks to be a rite older than Christianity that continued into historical times even though clergy opposed it. Legend says the goddess Brigit invented it after her son Ruadán fell in battle. It was a women's ritual. The women wailed and beat their hands above the body. Keeners were village women skilled in woeful melodies. Wives and daughters could sit in at the keening too.

okr.objective: keening is the Irish ritual of mourning for the dead.
key_results: Keening is an Irish mourning rite for the dead.
